headline: Granted variances for 60 Longmeadow Road and 32 Dunham Road, withdrew two applications, and continued a cell tower request
summary: The board heard and granted two variance requests, one for a two-bay garage at 60 Longmeadow Road and one for retail, storage, and office use at 32 Dunham Road. The board allowed the applicant at 26 Mason Street to withdraw a garage/ADU variance request and allowed the applicant at 21 Bridge Street to withdraw a lot subdivision variance request, both without prejudice. A special permit and variance request for a wireless facility at 12 Tozer Road was continued to May 27, 2026, and the March 25, 2026 minutes were approved.
decisions: Granted a Variance at 60 Longmeadow Road for a two-bay garage addition encroaching into the side yard setback, 4-0.
Granted a Variance at 32 Dunham Road to allow 9,000 sq. ft. of retail use by Boston Consignment and 12,000 sq. ft. for storage and office use, 4-0.
Allowed the applicant to withdraw the application at 26 Mason Street without prejudice, 4-0.
Accepted the written request to withdraw the application at 21 Bridge Street without prejudice, 4-0.
Accepted the written request to continue the application at 12 Tozer Road to the May 27, 2026 meeting, subject to signing the Waiver and Agreement, 4-0.
Approved the March 25, 2026 meeting minutes as written, 4-0.
plain_text:
CITY of BEVERLY
Zoning Board of Appeals
April 22, 2026 at 7:00 pm
These minutes are not a verbatim transcript of the public hearing of the Board of Appeals.  
Reviews of these Minutes or outcome of the public hearing should include an examination of the 
Board’s decision for that hearing.  
Members Present: Will Cosmas, Chairperson, Michael Barone, Cory Farinella, 
Laura Meisenhelter
Member Absent: Benjamin Roy
Others Present:     Jim Butler, Building Commissioner
Leanna Harris, Administrative Assistant
Location:       Council Chambers City Hall, 191 Cabot Street, Beverly
Will Cosmas began the meeting at 7:03pm and introduced the Board members present.
NEW PUBLIC HEARINGS
John Claiborne
requests a Variance to build a two-bay garage addition off the side of their existing home 
encroaching into the side yard setback. The property is located at 60 Longmeadow Road in the 
R10 zoning district. 
Robert Freni (Architect) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant and stated that the 
applicant seeks to build a two-bay garage. Mr. Freni provided an overview of the existing carport
that is 11’ from the existing home and the related plans.  The existing carport would be 
demolished and an existing shed on the property will be relocated.  The proposed project location
is in the northeast corner of the lot and the proposed extension would be on the east side of the 
property.  According to Mr. Freni, the existing lot is nonconforming in the R10 district, 
containing 7,500 sq. ft., where it should be 10,000 sq. ft. and having 70’ of frontage where 100’ 
is required.  Mr. Freni stated that the applicant has tried to keep the new garage width as minimal
as possible to prevent coming too close to the lot line.  According to Mr. Freni, the applicant 
wants to age in place and to be able to pull cars into the garage and go into the house.  The 
existing curb cut would remain the same. 
The existing carport is 6” below the roof line.  Mr. Freni stated that the plan is to have the new 
garage be level with the existing roofline of the house, and the existing entrance will remain.
Page 2 of 5
Mr. Freni stated the applicant has met with neighbors including the neighbor most affected on the
right side and they have submitted a letter in favor of the application.
Albert Turner, 26 Mason St. stated that his mother is an abutter and he thinks the plan is great 
and it is a good idea.
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved to close the public hearing.  
Mr. Cosmas seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
Mr. Farinella stated the request seems pretty straightforward and with the shape of the land there 
are not many options.  Mr. Cosmas stated he appreciates that the applicant has made the garage 
narrower than comfort would require in order to request the minimum relief.
MOTION:  Mr. Farinella moved to GRANT a Variance at 60 Longmeadow Road to 
build a two-bay garage addition off the side of their existing home encroaching into the 
side yard setback, due to the shape and size of the lot creating a hardship, subject to the 
plans submitted.  Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
Alexander & Femino o/b/o Joseph P. Coughlin, Trustee of
Gateway II Trust of 1997
requests a Variance to allow approximately 9,000 sq.ft. of the existing building on site to be 
used by Boston Consignment for retail purposes (70% of the business is conducted online) 
together with 12,000 sq. ft. for associated storage and office use. The use will be conducted in a 
part of the 51,158 sq. ft. existing building. The property is located at 32 Dunham Road in the IR 
zoning district. 
Thomas Alexander, Esq. (Alexander & Femino) addressed the Board on behalf of the applicant 
and stated that the applicant has owned this property since 2020.  According to Atty. Alexander, 
the history of the building dates back 50 years as a newspaper facility used be the Salem News 
and before that the Beverly Times, and the building was designed and built for retail use by the 
Beverly Times.
According to Atty. Alexander, the building consists of one story and is located on 6 acres in the 
IR district (industrial restricted).  Atty. Alexander stated that this particular zoning district does 
allow the uses that they are proposing, and dimensionally, this lot is considerably underutilized 
as far as what the maximum use could be.  Atty. Alexander stated that this lot has 6 acres with 
440’ of frontage on Dunham Road and it abuts residential neighborhoods and compliments the 
neighborhood well.  
According to Atty. Alexander, in July 2020 the Zoning Board approved a variance for a store 
called the Tile Source to operate at the property, so a retail use already exists on site, and in
Page 3 of 5
August 2020, the Zoning Board also approved a variance for Trout Movers to operate at this site.
Atty. Alexander stated the proposed use is for Boston Consignment where 70% of its business is 
conducted online. It will not generate much traffic; it is a minimal use of the property.
No one spoke in favor or against.
MOTION:  Ms. Meisenhelter moved to close the public hearing.  
Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
Mr. Cosmas cited the claim that 70% of Boston Consignment’s business is conducted online and 
asked what that means for traffic volume for the 30% of its business.  Stacy Lai (Boston 
Consignment) stated they are open 10-3pm.  According to Ms. Lai, there is usually one person 
walking in to represent a few homes and then there are browsers walking through. Ms. Lai 
estimates maybe 10 people each day.  Mr. Cosmas asked if there are people coming in to consign
and Ms. Lai stated that part of the business is all appointment based; no one comes in 
unannounced. 
Mr. Barone asked if Boston Consignment is generally open to the public and Ms. Lai replied that
it is from 10-3pm.
Mr. Cosmas stated he likes to see the building put to good use and that, in his opinion, the 
applicant seeks a minor use variance.  Mr. Barone stated he agrees, and he doesn’t anticipate the 
proposed use to result in high traffic volume.
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved to GRANT a Variance at 32 Dunham Road to allow 
approximately 9,000 sq. ft. of the existing building on site to be used by Boston 
Consignment for retail purposes (70% of the business is conducted online) together with 
12,000 sq. ft. for associated storage and office use. The use will be conducted in a part of 
the 51,158 sq. ft. existing building due to the special circumstances of the building that 
was developed and previously used for retail purposes, subject to the plans submitted.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARINGS
Albert Turner
requests a Variance to construct a new detached single-car garage with an Accessory Dwelling 
Unit (ADU) above, in accordance with Sections 300-36 D(6), D(8) of the Beverly Zoning 
Ordinance.  The property is located at 26 Mason Street in the RMD zoning district.  
Bill Nolan (Savoie Nolan Architects) provided revised plans for the applicant and stated that the
Page 4 of 5
applicant now would like to construct a garage with storage above without the prior ADU 
component contained in his initial application.  According to Mr. Nolan, the applicant works on a
classic car and would like to store it in the proposed garage.  Access to the storage area would be 
through a pull down only. There would be no windows other than on the front of the garage 
addition.
Mr. Nolan stated that the applicant seeks to match the width of the garage in his new plans; 
however the depth is insufficient, so they plan is to pull the garage forward in order to make it 
more useable.  The existing deck and rear door on the existing home needs to be removed to give
them the space to bring it forward.  
Mr. Nolan reviewed the revised plans with the Board.  The revised plans maintain a minimum of 
4’ to get around the garage, and all windows have been removed from the sides and rear of the 
second story, which will be a simple gambrel structure for storage space with 2 windows on the 
front for natural light and street presence. 
Mr. Nolan provided signatures from 8 abutters who have signed in favor of the revised proposal, 
including the rear that expressed the most concerns about the previous plans at the Board’s 
previous meeting.
No one spoke in favor or against.
Mr. Butler stated he did not realize that the applicant’s revised plans included removing the ADU
piece, which means the proposed construction also would need Variance relief from the 
accessory building section in the Zoning Ordinance.  Mr. Butler asked what the proposed 
structure’s height is and Mr. Nolan replied that, per the plans, it is 20.5’.  According to Mr. 
Butler, that would require variances from Sections 300-27 E(2), E(3), E(4) of the Beverly Zoning
Ordinance. Mr. Butler confirmed that the applicant would need to file a new application for that 
relief, which was not contained in the initial application under consideration.
Mr. Nolan requested that the applicant be permitted to withdraw the pending application without 
prejudice. 
MOTION: Mr. Barone moved to allow the applicant to withdraw the application at 26 
Mason Street, without prejudice.  Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
Jason Irving/21 Bridge Street LLC
request a Variance to subdivide the lot, retain the existing single-family home and subdivide the 
existing lot to create a new second lot for the construction of an additional single-family home.  
The addition of another single-family home to the lot would be consistent with the general 
character and other lot sizes in the neighborhood.  The property is located at 21 Bridge Street in 
the R10 zoning district.
Page 5 of 5
Prior to the meeting, the applicant submitted a written request to withdraw the application, 
without prejudice.
MOTION: Mr. Farinella moved to accept the written request to withdraw the application 
at 21 Bridge Street, without prejudice.  Ms. Meisenhelter seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless and the Towers, LLC 
requests a Special Permit under §§300-42 (C)(1)(p) and 300-91 height and setback Variances 
from §300-25A to permit a wireless communications facility with a monopole 124 feet in height 
(including 4' lightning rod) and setback from the property line of approximately 52'.  The 
property is located at 12 Tozer Road in the IR zoning district, Map 68, Parcel 25B.  
Prior to the meeting, the applicant submitted a written request to continue the application to the 
May 27, 2026 meeting of the Zoning Board.
MOTION:  Mr. Cosmas moved to accept the written request to continue the application 
at 12 Tozer Road to the May 27, 2026 meeting, subject to signing the Waiver and 
Agreement. Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
OTHER BUSINESS
A. Approval of March 25, 2026 Meeting Minutes (Cosmas)
MOTION: Ms. Meisenhelter moved to approve the March 25, 2026 meeting minutes as 
written and presented.  Mr. Farinella seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
MOTION: Ms. Meisenhelter moved to adjourn the meeting at 8:06p.m. 
Mr. Barone seconded the Motion.
Votes in favor: 4-0 (Cosmas, Barone, Farinella, Meisenhelter)
Motion carries.
Leanna Harris, Administrative Assistant
        Board of Appeals of the Zoning Ordinance
